newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Nov 6.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - Inflation fears knocked London shares again after the Bank of England's warning that higher interest rates would be needed to control inflation wiped out much of the market's early U.S. election-inspired gains. Shares immediately lost ground and the FTSE 100, up 25.4 points at the day's best, closed 14.6 points higher at 3,935.7.

FRANKFURT - German shares end bourse trade higher, boosted by Clinton's election victory and Republicans maintaining control of Congress. Overnight Wall Street gains helped market sentiment. The 30-share DAX ended 37.90 points, or 1.41 percent up at 2,729.19. In post-bourse trade the index was up 19.12 at 2,735.28.

PARIS - French shares finished at a high for the year, following a run up on bonds and the Dow. The markets' welcome to Bill Clinton's presidential re-election sparked a buying spree in Paris, with a massive 7.3 billion francs of turnover. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 26.05 points or 1.19 percent at 2,213.37.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed near the day's highs in sizeable volumes after a positive Wall Street opening helped the shares overcome a late bout of weakness. The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 16.27 points, or 0.67 percent, to close at 2,442.86. TOKYO - Japan's key stock index surged to end just below 21,000, relieved by Bill Clinton's re-election as U.S. president and the Republicans' retention of control in Congress. The market's next focus will be the announcement of Japan's new cabinet members. The Nikkei 225 average soared 399.19 points, or 1.94 percent, to finish at 20,991.52.

HONG KONG - Election fever swept Hong Kong stocks to record levels as investors viewed the results of the U.S. election as a promise of stable economic policy and looked forward to a rally in U.S. stocks. The Hang Seng index of blue chip stocks jumped to a new intra-day high of 12,779.11 before closing 272.77 points higher at a record close of 12,775.47.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed barely changed after a widely-expected cut in Australian official interest rates failed to excite investors. The maintenance of the political status quo in the United States after national elections also failed to stir interest and the All Ordinaries index closed a point lower at 2,360.6.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks fell for the third day running on Wednesday as anxieties over the recent weakness of the rand and confusion over government policy on exchange controls darkened the market's mood. The all-share index fell 50.1 points to 6,873.9 as industrials tumbled 56.9 points to 8,091.5. The gold index finished at 1,702.0, down 2.19 percent or 38.1 points.
